title: Overlay mesh shawl
subtitle: Surface overlay stitches worked across a lace mesh ground in fingering weight.
excerpt: An overlay mesh shawl has two layers of crochet: a lace mesh ground worked first, then a second layer of surface stitches worked on top to create a raised geometric pattern. The result looks woven from a distance and lacework close up.
sourceNotes: Overlay crochet technique developed in the late 20th century as an extension of traditional surface crochet, itself documented from the early 20th century. This shawl pattern is original to Homemade.

glossaryTerms.definition: A two-layer crochet technique where a foundation mesh ground is worked first, then a second set of stitches is worked on top by inserting the hook into specific mesh spaces to create a raised surface pattern.
A stitch worked on top of completed crochet by inserting the hook through the fabric from front to back and pulling up a loop, without using the foundation chain or stitches below.
The underlying open fabric of chains and single stitches that serves as the canvas for overlay crochet.
Wetting the finished shawl and pinning to stated dimensions so both layers set together.

crochet.gaugeText: 18 mesh sts x 12 rows = 10 x 10 cm in fingering weight with a 3.5 mm hook, blocked.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Triangular shawl, 160 cm wingspan x 75 cm deep at centre back, blocked.

content.text: An overlay mesh shawl is made in two passes. In the first pass you work a triangular
mesh ground
of chains and trebles from the top down, increasing at each edge to build the triangle. In the second pass you work
surface stitches
across the ground using a contrasting or matching yarn to create the
overlay mesh
pattern on top of the foundation.

The overlay gives the fabric a raised geometric quality: diamonds, chevrons, or grid lines appear to float above the lace mesh below. The work is advanced because you must read both the mesh grid and the overlay chart simultaneously.
What you need

items.name: Fingering weight yarn, main colour (MC)
items.substitutions: A smooth single-ply or lightly plied fingering in wool or cotton works best for the ground.

items.name: Fingering weight yarn, contrast colour (CC)
items.substitutions: Can also use MC for a tone-on-tone effect.

content.text: Gauge
18 mesh sts x 12 rows = 10 x 10 cm in fingering weight with a 3.5 mm hook, blocked. Work the gauge swatch in the MC only. The overlay adds body but does not significantly change the dimensions.
Phase 1: mesh ground
ch: chain
tr (UK): treble
Mesh square: 1 tr, ch 2, skip 2, 1 tr
Foundation: ch 7. Work (2 tr, ch 2, 2 tr) into 5th ch from hook. Turn. This is the centre spine.

Increase row: Ch 5. 1 tr into first tr (left edge increase). Work mesh squares across to spine. Work (2 tr, ch 2, 2 tr) into spine ch-2 space. Continue mesh to end. Work (1 tr, ch 2, 1 tr) into turning ch space (right edge increase). Turn.
Repeat increase row until
mesh ground
is 75 cm deep. Block the ground lightly before working overlay.
Phase 2: overlay
Attach CC at the top right corner of the blocked mesh ground. Insert hook from front to back through the first mesh square. Pull up a loop (
surface stitch
start). Ch 1 to anchor.

Diamond overlay repeat: *Cross diagonally up-right across 2 mesh squares (skip one, insert into the second). Cross diagonally down-right 2 squares. This makes one diamond half.* Continue across, building diamonds that are 4 squares wide and 4 rows tall. At each row of the ground, secure the overlay thread with a slip stitch before continuing the diagonal.
Work the overlay across the full width of the ground. Fasten off CC at the left edge. Reattach at the top of the next overlay row and repeat.
Blocking
After overlay is complete, soak the full shawl and block to 160 x 75 cm.
Blocking
melds both layers together. Pin the overlay threads gently so they sit flat against the ground without pulling.

attrs.heading: Common problems
attrs.intro: Overlay shawls have unique two-layer challenges.

items.fix: Work overlay stitches with a hook one size larger than the ground hook. The surface thread should lie on the fabric without gathering the mesh underneath.

items.cause: Losing track of the mesh square count
items.fix: Count mesh squares in the ground before working and mark every 4th square with a removable marker. Overlay diamonds sit on multiples of 4.

items.cause: Working in long runs without securing
items.fix: Work overlay in short segments of 10 diamonds at a time. Cut CC and rejoin rather than carrying it across long distances.
